A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uni3R work, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning supplementary material; v4 includes Appendix 6. Comparisons concern the material actually supplied.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, segmentation, depth-estimation and ablation results in Tables 1–6 and qualitative figures.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional benchmark comparisons, confidence-mask ablations and training-stability evidence, including in its appendix.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the intrinsic embedding, cross-view transformer, Gaussian and semantic prediction heads, rendering procedure, and photometric, semantic and confidence-masked geometry losses. Equations 1–13 remain unchanged; the additional explanations and experiments do not establish an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: v4 adds zero-shot evaluation on Mip-NeRF360 under two- and eight-view settings (Table 5). ScanNet, ScanNet++, RE10K, ACID and DTU were already described as training or evaluation datasets in v1; the appendix supplies DTU/ScanNet++ results rather than establishing newly introduced dataset coverage.

E2.justification: AnySplat is added to the retained ScanNet comparison and the four/eight-view RE10K and ScanNet comparisons (Tables 1 and 4). It also supplies the comparator for the new Mip-NeRF360 experiment. The other comparator memberships in corresponding retained experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The view-count experiment changes from a fixed-range four/eight/sixteen-view study (v1 Table 5) to a two/four/eight-view arbitrary-view model evaluation (v4 Table 6), which omits the inlier-ratio metric. v4 also adds two/eight-view Mip-NeRF360 testing. The stated 1,565-scene training set, 40-scene ScanNet evaluation and 256×256 resolution remain unchanged; newly supplied schedules do not establish changes to retained experiments.

E4.justification: v4 adds a confidence-mask sensitivity study comparing 70%, 90% and 100% retention with no geometry loss (Table 9), and a four-view training trajectory demonstrating collapse without geometry regularization (Figure 5). It replaces the controlled view-count analysis with arbitrary-view model evaluation and adds another qualitative reconstruction example. The original module ablation survives unchanged as Table 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The confidence-mask study concerns pixel reliability, and the new training curves do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds AnySplat, Mip-NeRF360, DTU/ScanNet++, confidence-mask and arbitrary-view results. Table 2 revises Uni3R's reported eight-view PSNR from 24.12 to 24.71 and sixteen-view depth error/inlier ratio from 5.88/42.88 to 3.97/60.48. However, Appendix Table 10 retains the earlier depth values, leaving an internal discrepancy. The replacement view-count results use a different reported experiment and cannot establish same-setting gains; Table 3 and the original module-ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, rendering expressions and loss formulations in Equations 1–13 are retained. Neither the revised main text nor the appendix introduces new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains unified, feed-forward reconstruction and semantic understanding from unposed multi-view images. v4 extends the abstract's state-of-the-art claim explicitly to out-of-domain Mip-NeRF360 and adds training stabilization as an explicit purpose of the geometric loss in the introduction.

C2.justification: v4 explains the geometric loss as preventing unstable optimization and collapse, and attributes improvement over LSeg to multi-view spatial fusion filtering inconsistent predictions. It also replaces the earlier monotonic improvement-with-more-views interpretation with an arbitrary-view usability argument. These refine the explanation of the retained method without introducing a new limitations analysis.

D1.justification: Appendix 6.4 supplies previously unavailable checkpoint initialization, learning rates, training durations, warmups, per-GPU batch sizes and mixed-view sampling details. Section 6.3 specifies the depth inlier threshold of 1.03. The direct repository link is replaced with a project-page link, without establishing changed resource availability. Hardware reporting becomes inconsistent: the main text retains the all-A100 statement, while the appendix specifies H100s for multi-view RE10K training.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to AnySplat, Mip-NeRF360, Pointmap Association and Piecewise-Plane Constraint, Compact 3D Gaussian Representation, and F-3DGS. AnySplat becomes an explicit empirical comparison, but the central positioning relative to DUSt3R, LSM, UniForward and scene-specific semantic reconstruction remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 revises the abstract, geometry-loss motivation, experimental interpretations and conclusion, and updates author information. It introduces numbered method subheadings, a separate analysis subsection and an appendix. Most introductory, related-work and architectural prose retains the earlier narrative and wording.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: the synthesis and segmentation figures exchange order, the synthesis grid gains a fourth example, and the architecture diagram is rearranged. New benchmark and appendix tables and a training-stability plot are added, while the view-count table changes structure. The document template, typography and placement of results relative to references also change.

improvement.justification: The added confidence-mask and training-stability evidence strengthens support for the geometric regularizer, while explicit training schedules improve reproducibility. Additional comparisons make generalization claims more assessable. These gains are qualified by conflicting depth values in Tables 2 and 10, inconsistent hardware descriptions, and broad superiority language despite mixed Mip-NeRF360 metrics in Table 5. The original controlled view-count analysis is also lost. Overall, the added support and documentation provide a modest net improvement.
